clue.text: With steady progress, transfer control to Duke

parts.note: to hand over is to pass control to someone else
dukes is old slang for fists, so a duke is a fist

explanation.surface: An instruction to pass power smoothly to a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' looks like a nobleman, but 'dukes' is slang for fists ('put up your dukes'), so a duke is a FIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Making money hand over fist means gaining it rapidly and continuously, the idiom for steady progress.

clue.text: New house I had moved into is ghastly

indicators.note: moved into says one piece goes inside the other
new says the letters of house are made anew

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A new house someone has moved into turns out ghastly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal and 'moved into' the container signal; the surface reads them as a family moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideous means extremely ugly or horrible.

clue.text: 4, for example, is by no means old

definitions.meaning: 4 down is Eric, or Little by Little, a Victorian school story, a book of fiction

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points at 4 down, ERIC, whose clue 'Little by little' is the subtitle of Farrar's 1858 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric is a work of long fiction; novel also means new and original.

clue.text: Sir Lucius seen round high-class part of boat

indicators.note: seen round means the character surrounds a letter

parts.note: Sir Lucius O'Trigger is the duelling Irishman in Sheridan's play The Rivals
U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A knight spotted near the posh end of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: U puts U, 'upper-class', after the O of O'TRIGGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrigger is a float or frame projecting from a boat's side for stability.

clue.text: Little by little, cut shrub

indicators.note: cut means the shrub's name loses its last letter

parts.note: erica is the heather genus, a shrub

explanation.surface: Gradually trimming back a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little by little' looks like an adverb, but it is the title of a book: Eric, or Little by Little.
explanation.definitionFit: Farrar's novel is called Eric, or Little by Little, so its subtitle stands for its title.

clue.text: Occasion for celebration calling for fast live broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebration needs a quick live transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival is a day or period of celebration.

clue.text: Boat strike

definitions.meaning: a small fishing vessel with a sail

explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a single-masted fishing boat; to smack is to slap.

clue.text: Girl with fuel that's used for cooking

parts.note: Olive is a girl's name
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A woman with a can of fuel in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is a common cooking fat pressed from olives.

clue.text: Mindlessly repeat standard rubbish

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Thoughtlessly repeating the usual nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to echo words without understanding, as the bird does.

clue.text: Formal wear on peacemaker fits exactly

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a dove is the symbol of peace and a name for a conciliator
tails is a tailcoat, worn on formal occasions

explanation.surface: A diplomat's tailcoat is a perfect fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that dovetail interlock neatly, like a carpenter's joint, so they match perfectly.

clue.text: Entirely middle-of-the-road place in Scotland

parts.note: all means wholly or entirely

indicators.note: asks for the central letters of the word that follows, road

explanation.surface: A Scottish town that is completely moderate in its views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle-of-the-road' reads as 'moderate', but it splits: the middle of ROAD is OA. ALLOA is a small town in central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town on the River Forth in Clackmannanshire.

clue.text: Young lady I love returned well-used equipment

indicators.note: returned means everything before it is read back to front

parts.note: a girl is a young lady
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl's love comes back for some much-used kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns GIRL I O backwards to give OILRIG. The definition plays on 'well-used': equipment used at an oil well.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig is the structure used for drilling an oil well.

clue.text: Idle parasite finished off

parts.note: a tick is a blood-sucking parasite
over means done or finished off

explanation.surface: A lazy bloodsucker has been wiped out.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over runs slowly while not engaged, that is, it idles.

clue.text: Cheat by overpricing old beer

parts.note: to sting someone is to overcharge them

explanation.surface: A pub fleecing its customers on the price of its ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is an old name for a strong ale.

clue.text: Mussorgsky's introduction is certainly bold

parts.note: I'm, as in 'I'm so-and-so', is how one introduces oneself
Modest was the first name of Mussorgsky the composer

explanation.surface: The opening of a Mussorgsky work is certainly daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction' looks like a musical opening, but Mussorgsky's self-introduction would be 'I'm Modest', his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodest means forward or brazen, lacking shyness.

clue.text: Light support from a politician in Liberal position

indicators.note: in means the second group of pieces sits inside the first

parts.note: a post is a position or job
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A Liberal MP backing a policy from a strategic position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light support' looks abstract, but it is a post that holds up a street light.
explanation.definitionFit: A street lamp is mounted on a tall pole that holds it up.

clue.text: One who samples US author first, a minor literary figure

indicators.note: first means the author comes before the sampler

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
a taster samples food or drink

explanation.surface: A critic samples an American writer first.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is an inferior writer of verse.

clue.text: Plant succeeded with little peat mixture

parts.note: wee is Scots for little

indicators.note: mixture says the letters of peat are mixed up

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant thrived in a little peat mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet pea is a climbing flowering plant.

clue.text: School hero has to start to make toast

indicators.note: the start of the word make is its first letter

parts.note: to brown bread is to toast it

explanation.surface: A school's star pupil must begin making the toast.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Brown is the hero of the Victorian novel Tom Brown's Schooldays, set at Rugby School.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Brown is the boy protagonist of Thomas Hughes's public-school story.

clue.text: Covering for roof in the church being indicated

parts.note: that points to something being indicated

explanation.surface: Pointing out the roofing on a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reed used as roofing.

clue.text: Cowardly way to express pain

parts.note: a yell is a loud way to voice a feeling
ow is the cry someone gives when hurt

explanation.surface: A timid person's way of showing they are hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for lacking courage.

clue.text: Pacific route used by Indians? On the contrary

definitions.text: Pacific route used by Indians? On the contrary

parts.words: Pacific route used by Indians? On the contrary
parts.note: the opposite of a peaceful path is one taken by Native Americans going to fight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' looks like the ocean but means peaceful; the contrary of a peaceful route is a hostile one.
explanation.definitionFit: The warpath was the route of Native American warriors heading to battle.

clue.text: Include one caught by chap, firmly hooked

parts.note: to add is to include
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Ted is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A fisherman's catch firmly on the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone addicted is dependent on a habit, unable to give it up.

clue.text: Warm applause

definitions.meaning: to comfort or gladden, as in to warm someone's heart

explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to hearten them; a cheer is a cry of acclaim.

clue.text: Smart fisherman?

definitions.meaning: one who daps, dapping being fishing by bobbing a fly on the water surface

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a made-up word: someone who daps.
explanation.definitionFit: Dapper means neatly turned out; to dap is to fish with a bouncing fly.

clue.text: Dish has edge pointed up with gold

indicators.note: in a down clue, pointed up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a lip is an edge or rim
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A plate with its rim turned up and gilded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointed up' turns LIP to PIL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a spiced rice dish.

clue.text: Bird seen, not heard

indicators.note: heard means the word not is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word not as spoken

explanation.surface: A bird you can see but not hear, like a well-behaved child.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'children should be seen and not heard'.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a wading bird of the sandpiper family.

clue.text: Social class in form associated with East

parts.note: a cast is a form or mould

explanation.surface: A social class shaped by eastern influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social rank, as in the traditional Hindu system.

clue.text: Smoke coming from Spanish dish turning brown inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece goes within the dish

parts.note: paella is the rice dish of Valencia

indicators.note: turning means the word for brown is read backwards

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Smoke rising from a paella as it browns in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' is the reversal signal and 'inside' the container signal. 'Smoke' is a noun here: something you smoke, a thin cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long slim cigar, something smoked.

clue.text: Significant advance the rest completed

parts.note: a break is a rest
through means finished or completed

explanation.surface: A big step forward once the remainder is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakthrough is an important discovery or development.
